# Incident Report — 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 192.168.1.216 |
| MAC address | 9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9 (ASUSTek network adapter) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 |
| AD domain | spoonwatch.net (DC: SPOONWATCH-DC, 192.168.1.2) |
| Logged-in user | steve.smith (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from both the workstation and the DC) |

DHCP lease at frame 1 (t=0.0s) confirms DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 requested 192.168.1.216 from the gateway; NBNS registrations for DESKTOP-GXNYNO2/SPOONWATCH corroborate the same host.

## Malware Family
**Behaviorally attributed to Vidar Stealer (Arkei/Vidar/Racoon-lineage Windows infostealer). Not signature-confirmed** — there was no AV/YARA/IDS engine run against this pcap, and no self-identifying string was found in the payloads. Attribution rests on strong behavioral fingerprint:

- Malware downloaded four legitimate Mozilla NSS cryptography DLLs disguised with `.jpg` extensions and served with `Content-Type: image/jpeg`: **nss3.dll, softokn3.dll, freebl3.dll, mozglue.dll** (plus msvcp140.dll/vcruntime140.dll runtime deps). These NSS libraries are the standard toolset stealers bundle to decrypt Firefox/Thunderbird-stored saved logins — they serve no purpose for a legitimate browser update.
- HTTP requests to the C2 carried **no User-Agent header** and a fixed `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, `Accept-Charset: iso-8859-1, utf-8, utf-16` header set — consistent with a non-browser HTTP client library, not a real browser.
- Final exfiltration upload was a ZIP archive (filename `_5861695120.zip`, the classic Vidar naming convention `_<numeric>.zip`) containing the canonical Vidar loot-folder layout: `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/`, `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt`.
- C2 contacted by raw IP literal with **no preceding DNS lookup**, evading domain-based detection.

## Indicators of Compromise

### Command-and-Control
- **C2 endpoint:** `2.56.57.108:80` (HTTP, IP-literal, no associated hostname — no DNS query preceded the connection)
- Server banner: `Apache/2.4.12 (Win32) OpenSSL/1.0.1m PHP/5.3.29 mod_wsgi/4.4.11 Python/2.7.10`
- No malicious domain observed — the actor used a bare IP address specifically to avoid a DNS-based IOC.

### Malicious URLs (all to 2.56.57.108, first contact at t=202.9s / ~3:23 into capture)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` — payload DLL retrieval (POST-then-download gate)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php` — checkpoint/gate call
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` — final exfiltration upload (POST, 379,629 bytes)

### Files Transferred (downloaded to victim, disguised as .jpg, actually Win32 PE DLLs)
| URL | Actual file type | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|
| /osk//1.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) | 16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660 |
| /osk//2.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — freebl3.dll | a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba |
| /osk//3.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — mozglue.dll | 3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd |
| /osk//4.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) — msvcp140.dll | 334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4 |
| /osk//5.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — nss3.dll (1.2 MB) | e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78 |
| /osk//6.jpg | PE32 DLL (GUI) — softokn3.dll | 43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083 |
| /osk//7.jpg | PE32 DLL (console) — vcruntime140.dll | c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d |

### Exfiltrated Data (uploaded from victim to C2, final POST to /osk/)
- **File name:** `_5861695120.zip` (Content-Type: `zip`, 379,629-byte multipart body)
- **SHA256 of raw upload capture:** 1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f
- **Archive contents (10 files, 539,698 bytes uncompressed):**
  - `autofill/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `autofill/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt` — saved form autofill data
  - `cc/Google Chrome_Default.txt`, `cc/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt` — saved payment card fields (empty in this instance)
  - `cookies/Google Chrome_Network.txt` (137,885 bytes), `cookies/Microsoft Edge_Default.txt` (126,732 bytes) — full browser cookie stores
  - `outlook.txt` — Outlook account/profile data
  - `passwords.txt` — saved browser credentials (decrypted via the NSS DLL set above)
  - `screenshot.jpg` (271,977 bytes) — desktop screenshot at time of theft
  - `system.txt` — host/system fingerprint

## Timeline
- t=0s: DESKTOP-GXMYNO2 boots, DHCP-obtains 192.168.1.216, joins spoonwatch.net domain (Kerberos to DC 192.168.1.2 as steve.smith)
- t≈202.9s: First and only contact with C2 2.56.57.108:80 begins
- t≈203–205s: Seven fake-.jpg payload DLLs (NSS/browser-decryption toolkit) downloaded sequentially
- t≈205s: `main.php` gate call
- t≈207.7s: Final 379 KB exfiltration ZIP uploaded to `/osk/`; C2 replies with empty `200 text/html` ack
- Remainder of the ~751-second capture: only legitimate Windows Update / Microsoft telemetry traffic — no further C2 or exfil activity observed

## Note on Initial Access
No dropper, phishing artifact, or exploit traffic precedes the first C2 contact within this capture — the stealer was already resident and executing when packet capture began. Initial infection vector cannot be determined from this pcap alone.
